label: adult-s2
summary: The model is mostly a linear score on the logit scale: replacing its direct terms by their mean lowers training AUC from 0.9064 to 0.6458, while switching all the hidden parts off together lowers it to 0.8873. Being married to a civilian spouse (-1.75 per sd) and capital gain (-1.99 per sd) are strong direct terms lowering the predicted probability of the lower income class. On top of that score, education lowers the predicted probability more steeply from high-school graduation upward (the largest hidden part: AUC 0.8959 without it); capital gain switches on a second, steep downward slope past a threshold between 4500 US dollars and 5000 US dollars, adding -8.85 to the score on average for the 2042 training rows past it; and a gate open for husbands adds 0.75 on average for the 15748 husbands, giving back to them part of the marriage term. A missing occupation adds 1.27 for 2231 rows and machine operators get a small step up (0.51 on average for 2417 rows). The census sampling weight and a near-constant some-college part barely matter (training AUC without them: 0.9064 and 0.9064, against 0.9064 with them), and two units are off on every training row (the Peru unit: 0 rows on; the unit after the some-college unit: 0 rows on). Two small regimes are fitted to few rows: workclass without employment history (9 rows, pushed to a predicted lower-income probability of above 99%) and a Taiwan birthplace (49 rows). The annotated model reproduces the network on every training row to within 6.7e-16.

The 47 unchecked free-text sentences are prose without numbers (predictions, domain readings, structural statements such as 'no part feeds another', which holds by construction: every hidden exit goes to the output or to a unit inside its own leaf). Category labels come from the tools' codebook (e.g. workclass=4 'private'); training prevalences of the one-hot columns match the alphabetical Adult coding. The outcome (risk) is the lower income class, so negative weights lower the predicted probability of earning at most the threshold.
tool_bugs: No tool failures. Notes: (1) query_ablate(direct=true) reports no direct edges after add_identity_node on the output, so direct weights were read with query_ablate(edges=[...->identity_0]). (2) query_enumerate refuses this genome (age has 74 values), so 'every level' claims use query_probe sweeps over each level of the one categorical input involved, plus query_subgroup counts of 0. (3) The active-count lint reads 'on for N rows' about a subset (rows below a threshold) as the unit's total active count and refuses it; reworded. (4) The scope-word lint flags category labels such as 'never worked' / 'never married' in evidence descriptions; reworded. (5) get_formula returns no provenance id, so formulas were attached as analytical_formula payloads (LaTeX) without a query_id.
